full_judgment: 11. Having placed the Civil Revision, Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury along with Mr Iqbal Kalam Chowdhury and Mr Shahin Miraz Choudhury, learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the Court of Appeal below failed to consider that following the proceeding of SA Miscellaneous Case No.39 of 1979-1980, the DS Khatians, Exhibit-Ka series was prepared but, the initiation and conclusion of the said SA Miscellaneous Case No.39 of 1979-1980 have no basis as regarding such claim that the land belonged to the police department was not proved by producing any document while even, said DS Khatian was not legally and formally proved and marked as Exhibits by the Court of Appeal below and, as such„ the judgment and decree of the Court of Appeal below is liable to be declared to have been passed illegally and upon misreading the material evidence on records and thereby, the Court of Appeal below committed errors of law resulting in errors in the decree occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that apart from the certified copies of four DS Khatians, defendant Nos.1-3 could not produce any other document in support of the claim of the defendants. On the other hand, the plaintiffs produced all the relevant documents regarding the Settlement Cases and rent receipts and subsequent documents of title and accordingly, the Trial Court having meticulously perused and examined the material evidence on records rightly decreed the suit and on the contrary, the Court of Appeal below without reversing those material findings and observations of the Trial Court mechanically reversed and set-aside the judgment and decree of the Trial Court and thus, the judgment and decree of the Court of Appeal below being not a proper judgment and decree of reversal, the same is liable to be set-aside as thereby, the Court of Appeal below committed errors of law resulting in errors in the decree occasioning failure of justice. The Trial Court having considered the depositions of the PWs rightly came to the decision that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land either by constructing a dwelling house or by cultivation. On the other hand, the defendant-appellant could not prove their title and possession in the suit land but, the Court of Appeal below merely on surmise, conjecture and inference on four DS Khatians came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit land and thus, the judgment and decree of the Court of Appeal below suffer from non-application of judicial mind and misreading of material evidence on record and thereby, the Court of Appeal below committed errors of law resulting in errors in the decree occasioning failure of justice and hence, the Rule should be made absolute and the judgment and decree of the Court of Appeal below should be set-aside.
